title: The Grand Tour Renewed for Season Two With Its New Presenting Trio
excerpt:
Prime Video has ordered another season of the reinvented motoring series.
Francis Bourgeois, James Engelsman and Thomas Holland will return, with production planned for 2027.
body_md:
Prime Video has renewed the reimagined version of The Grand Tour for a second season, keeping Francis Bourgeois, James Engelsman and Thomas Holland in the driving seats. Studio Lambert is expected to begin production in 2027. The announcement confirms the streaming service's intention to continue the program beyond its first outing with the new presenters, although no premiere date has been announced.

The renewal marks another step in a particularly delicate transition for a long-running motoring brand. Jeremy Clarkson, James May and Richard Hammond fronted The Grand Tour between 2016 and 2024, building on the chemistry that had already made them household names through Top Gear. Their combination of road trips, competitive challenges and irreverent exchanges was central to the appeal of the series. Any successor lineup would inevitably face comparisons with that established partnership.

Bourgeois, Engelsman and Holland acknowledged the scale of that challenge in their response to the news. They said that taking on the job had felt more foolish than brave, even with the blessings of Clarkson, May and Hammond. The positive reception to their first season, they added, exceeded their expectations. With another installment now secured, the presenters hope to grow more comfortable in their roles and take greater creative risks while retaining the program's playful attitude.

Executive producer Nia Yemoh also pointed to the evolving chemistry among the hosts as a priority for the next season. She said the production team wants to explore more unexpected locations and stories, while preserving the competitive element that viewers associate with The Grand Tour. Her comments suggest continuity in the show's basic approach rather than a complete reinvention of its format, even as the personalities at its center have changed.

Studio Lambert's executive producers are Phil Churchward, Tim Harcourt, Stephen Lambert and Yemoh. Hilary Berkshire and Diana Focke are listed as production executives. Their involvement provides an established production team for the next installment, but the announcement does not identify specific destinations, vehicles, challenges or episode counts. Those details remain to be disclosed as the project moves toward filming.

Renewing a series after such a prominent change of presenters is a meaningful commitment. It gives the new team more time to establish its own identity instead of being judged solely against the previous hosts. Nevertheless, the renewal should not be confused with independently verified viewing figures or a guarantee that every longtime fan has embraced the changes. The announcement offers no detailed audience data, and its significance is primarily that Prime Video has authorized another season.

For now, the confirmed developments are straightforward: the same three presenters will return, Studio Lambert will produce the next season, and work is scheduled to start in 2027. Prime Video has not specified when the new episodes will arrive. Further claims about the route, format changes or release window would go beyond what has been announced.
